hypothesis: Separating open provider-symbol-side mechanisms by causal entry identity, marked economics, path excursion, and venue protection can improve portfolio research decisions without contaminating resolved performance or changing execution.
decision: Retain the provisional mechanism audit and add exact provider-native HIP-3 Swing attribution. Current GOLD-long and SNDK-short entries were provider-aligned across EMA, Heikin-Ashi, order-block, and eligible pivot state, so their adverse marks are not explained by random directional routing. Keep v25 execution, risk, sizing, and exits unchanged while both paths resolve. The next report-only strategy experiment should hold the eligible HIP-3 identity fixed and compare provider-onset entry with first-pullback and next-completed-bar confirmation, separated by asset and side with after-cost, missed-fill, and concentration evidence. This revision cannot place, close, resize, route, rank, gate, restart, or promote a strategy.
falsifier: The attribution is invalidated by any mismatch between recorded provider metrics and the normalized identity, treating legacy null HA or order-block values as aligned, a non-eligible pivot label, open marks entering resolved performance, changed evidence bytes, or execution authority. The timing recommendation should be revised if the current paths resolve favorably without timing-related adverse excursion, or if a causal timing comparison fails to improve after-cost outcomes across assets and both sides without largest-winner dependence.
limitations: Only three resolved HIP-3 Swing lifecycles have provider-native attribution.
The full-metric SPCX winner and legacy partial loss occurred at different times and do not isolate a feature effect.
GOLD and SNDK are open and their marked economics can reverse.
Pivot confirmation is derived from an eligible provider decision because the legacy readiness payload does not expose pivot state as a structured metric.
The ignored HA-flip evidence contains two open and one resolved commodity lifecycle and cannot select an exit policy.
No live process, route, order, stop, target, position, size, allocation, leverage, or exit policy changed.
